pairs.subject: prompt-assembly
pairs.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/intake.py:307 The intake assembler that the message route calls keeps only the last 48 turns and renders them under 'CONVERSATION SO FAR' with no line saying earlier turns were left out, so a long session shows the model a partial history that looks complete (the earlier stale verdict still holds).

techniques.evidence: pipeline/jobfit/intake.py:1677 The windowed transcript is labelled as the whole conversation and the omitted count is never stated. The model only sees absolute [N] indices. The attachment rung does it right: it marks its cut at line 1558.

app/api/intake/[id]/message/route.ts:143 The route hands typed inputs (transcript, brief, message, lang, attachments, dossier) to one engine assembler per family and never passes pre-rendered prompt text. The stable system brief is passed separately from the per-call prompt.

pipeline/jobfit/intake.py:1562 Third-party attachment text enters at one declared, fenced insertion point. The text is defused and labelled as reference data, not instructions. The requestor message has its own fence.

pipeline/jobfit/intake.py:44 The technique's own gates are not met. Intake dialogs rarely outgrow a 48-turn tail, and long-range continuity is carried by the accumulated RoleBrief, not by a summary pyramid.
pipeline/jobfit/intake.py:1686 The intake call grants no tools or operations, only an output schema, so there is no capability registry to document.

pairs.registryProposal: context-budgeting could name a softer variant of the 'silent partial view': absolute turn indices like [12] imply that earlier history exists, but they do not count as a notice. The rule should say whether an implied gap satisfies 'truncation names what it dropped'.
